title: "Try a model spec"
format:
  html:
    toc: true
execute:
  warning: false
  message: false
---

Refit the GAMM under alternative specifications and see how the effects move.
Each fit uses a subsample of the saved analysis data (half the rows within each model), so a fit takes about a minute.
Smaller subsamples are faster but unreliable: at 25% the Method x target variance collapses and every structure effect shrinks to zero.
Fits are cached to `output/diy/`; editing a formula under an existing label refits it.

Effects are on the log link, so `exp(value)` is the WIS ratio against the average: 1.2 is 20% worse than average.
Estimates on the subsample are close to, not identical with, the paper's. Set `frac = 1` in `load_diy_data()` to reproduce them exactly (about 100 s per fit; render detached, as in `CLAUDE.md`).

Requires `output/log/results.rds` and `output/natural/results.rds` from `model_wis()`.

```{r setup}
library(here)
source(here("R", "analysis-model.R")) # m.formula_joint
source(here("R", "utils-diy.R"))

data_log <- load_diy_data("log", frac = 0.5)
baseline <- fit_spec("baseline", m.formula_joint, data_log)
m.formula_joint
```

## 1. Adjustment

Method alone (with the target, since the Method cells are by target) against the full model.
The gap is what the adjustment set does to the structure estimates.
`Method_by_target` shows the cells behind each pooled effect.

```{r adjustment}
#| fig-height: 7
method_only <- fit_spec(
  "method only",
  wis ~ s(Method, Epi_target, bs = "re") + Epi_target,
  data_log
)
compare_specs(list(baseline, method_only), c("Method", "Method_by_target"))
```

## 2. Drop one adjustment at a time

Which confounder moves the Method effects most?

```{r drop-one}
drop_terms <- list(
  "no location" = . ~ . - s(Location, bs = "re"),
  "no variant" = . ~ . - s(VariantPhase, bs = "re"),
  "no incidence" = . ~ . - s(Incidence),
  "no trend" = . ~ . - s(Trend, bs = "re")
)
dropped <- imap(drop_terms, \(term, label) {
  fit_spec(label, update(m.formula_joint, term), data_log)
})
compare_specs(c(list(baseline), dropped), "Method")
spec_stats(c(list(baseline), dropped))
```

## 3. Scoring scale

The same formula on WIS scored on the natural scale.
Natural-scale WIS grows with incidence, so large countries and peaks weigh more.

```{r scale}
data_natural <- load_diy_data("natural", frac = 0.5)
natural <- fit_spec("natural scale", m.formula_joint, data_natural)
compare_specs(list(baseline, natural), c("Method", "CountryTargets"))
```

## 4. Response family

Gaussian with a log link against the primary Tweedie.
A log-link Gaussian cannot start from scores of exactly zero, so this arm adds 1e-7 to every score, as `R/sensitivity/check-family.R` does.
See that script for why the primary fit is Tweedie.

```{r family}
data_offset <- load_diy_data("log", frac = 0.5, wis_offset = 1e-7)
gaussian_fit <- fit_spec("gaussian", m.formula_joint, data_offset,
                         family = gaussian(link = "log"))
compare_specs(list(baseline, gaussian_fit), "Method")
```

## 5. Horizon term

A model random effect with one shared horizon curve, against the primary per-model horizon deviations (`fs`).
The `fs` term shrinks models that forecast few horizons towards the shared curve.

```{r horizon}
#| fig-height: 10
model_re <- fit_spec(
  "model re",
  update(m.formula_joint,
         . ~ . - s(Horizon, Model, k = 4, bs = "fs") + s(Model, bs = "re")),
  data_log
)
compare_specs(list(baseline, model_re), "Model")
```

## Your own

Copy a chunk, change the `update()`, give it a new label.

```{r own}
#| eval: false
mine <- fit_spec("mine", update(m.formula_joint, . ~ . + s(Horizon, by = Epi_target, k = 4)), data_log)
compare_specs(list(baseline, mine), c("Method", "CountryTargets"))
```

## Fits

```{r stats}
spec_stats(c(list(baseline, method_only), dropped,
             list(natural, gaussian_fit, model_re)))
```
